svg.title: Find PostgreSQL connection details using pgAdmin
svg.desc: Illustration showing pgAdmin Server Properties Connection for host, port and username; Databases for the target database; the password issuer for the original database password; and Parameters for SSL mode. The maintenance database, pgAdmin master password and assumed role are distinguished from the app's fields.
svg.text: DATA MOVER · POSTGRESQL · PGADMIN
Find the connection details in pgAdmin
Use a working server registration and the login approved for Data Mover.
Right-click server → Properties → Connection
HOST NAME/ADDRESS
Database hostname or IP
PORT
Actual port (often 5432)
USERNAME
Approved database login
Use the login Username, not the server display name or a separate assumed Role. Close without changing settings.
Choose the actual database
Servers
↳ your server → Databases
↳ intended database
Maintenance database may be a different database.
A schema such as public is not the Database field.
Query Tool: SELECT current_database(), session_user, current_user;
Obtain the database password
Use the original secret from its issuer or
your approved secret manager.
pgAdmin master / web sign-in password ≠ DB password
Role Definition → Password sets or changes a password.
A saved pgAdmin connection does not recover the secret.
Do not reset a shared role to fill in the Data Mover form.
4 · REVIEW PROPERTIES → PARAMETERS → SSL MODE
Data Mover accepts require, verify-ca and verify-full. Provision any required certificate files on the app runtime.
Host, tunnel and certificate settings that work on your laptop may differ on Posit Connect.
Connections → Credentials → PostgreSQL → Save and test changes → Status
Illustration · reviewed October 22, 2026 · actual pgAdmin screenshots and source links are in the guide.
